events.title: Founding of Los Angeles
events.description: A group of 44 settlers, known as Los Pobladores, founded El Pueblo de Nuestra Señora la Reina de los Ángeles under Spanish colonial rule in Alta California.
events.significance: The settlement grew into Los Angeles, one of the largest and most influential cities in the United States and a global center of entertainment, trade, and culture.

events.title: Proclamation of the French Third Republic
events.description: After news of Napoleon III's capture at the Battle of Sedan reached Paris, the Second Empire collapsed and the Third Republic was proclaimed at the Hôtel de Ville.
events.significance: The Third Republic lasted until 1940 and became France's longest-lived government since 1789, establishing durable republican institutions.

events.title: Opening of the Pearl Street Station
events.description: Thomas Edison switched on the Pearl Street Station in lower Manhattan, the first commercial central power plant in the United States, supplying electric light to customers in the financial district.
events.significance: It marked the beginning of the commercial electric power industry and the widespread electrification of cities.

events.title: George Eastman Registers the Kodak Trademark
events.description: George Eastman registered the Kodak trademark and received a patent for his roll-film camera, which came preloaded with film and was marketed with the slogan 'You press the button, we do the rest.'
events.significance: The Kodak camera made photography accessible to the general public and launched popular amateur photography.

events.title: Founding of Google
events.description: Larry Page and Sergey Brin, Stanford PhD students, incorporated Google Inc. and began operating from a rented garage in Menlo Park, California.
events.significance: Google became the dominant internet search engine and grew into one of the world's most influential technology companies, reshaping how people access information.
